title: The Exit
subtitle: EPILOGUE · THE LAST CHOICE
opening: At the edge of the Machine, a control panel waits with two switches. Nothing here tells you which world is the original. You've learned to question what you see and to defend what you believe. But no argument can make this choice for you.
question: The Machine will honor one choice. What will your party do?

options.label: UNPLUG
options.text: Pull the plug and step into a world the Machine can't control.

options.label: STAY
options.text: Stay connected and build a life with the people and possibilities here.

votingNote: Choose for yourself. There's no right answer here. When everyone has voted, the result appears. If it's a tie, the host makes the final call after hearing everyone out.
tiePrompt: It's a tie. Both choices have good reasons behind them. Talk it through, then the host decides.

unplug.title: UNPLUG · The Unscripted Door
unplug.reflection: The plug slips free. Air brushes your skin. Maybe it's real; maybe it's another careful illusion. You walk anyway. You've chosen an unplanned world, where uncertainty is part of the life you build together.
reasons: Acting in a world no one designed for you may matter more than comfort or certainty.
Discovery, chance meetings, and being responsible for what happens can be valuable in themselves.
unplug.strongestObjection: The best case for STAY: experiences, commitments, and relationships in a virtual world might still be real and valuable. Leaving doesn't automatically make a life better.

stay.title: STAY · The World You Choose
stay.reflection: You leave the plug in. The garden past the panel fills with voices you know. The sky may be computed, but that alone doesn't make the friendships, work, and joy under it fake. You choose to take responsibility for the life you can live here.
reasons: A life can include knowledge, care, and meaningful work even in a virtual world.
Where an experience comes from doesn't by itself decide what it's worth.
stay.strongestObjection: The best case for UNPLUG: the Machine may limit what you can do and whom you can meet. Choosing freely and facing unscripted risks might matter a lot.

closingNote: These are the positions your party took in the challenges it won. They describe choices made under pressure, not labels for the players.
credits: Structure inspired by David Chalmers, *Reality+: Virtual Worlds and the Problems of Philosophy* (2022). Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.
